record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: Can integrable Hamiltonian systems be perturbed in a way that produces examples whose number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits has exactly quadratic growth?

evidence.quote: examples where the growth is exactly quadratic

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ be a symplectic manifold and $H: M \to \mathbb{R}$ a smooth Hamiltonian whose flow $\varphi_H^t$ is completely integrable, in the sense that there exist $n$ functionally independent Poisson-commuting smooth first integrals. A periodic orbit of $\varphi_H^t$ with prime period $T>0$ is called primitive, and two such orbits are geometrically distinct if their images in $M$ differ. For each $T>0$, let
$$N(T) \;=\; \#\bigl\{\text{geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of }\varphi_H^t\text{ with prime period} \le T\bigr\}.$$

Question. Does there exist a completely integrable Hamiltonian $H_0$ together with a smooth perturbation $H_\varepsilon = H_0 + \varepsilon K$ (with $\varepsilon$ small) such that the perturbed flow $\varphi_{H_\varepsilon}^t$ has exactly quadratic growth of its counting function, that is, there are constants $0 < c_1 \le c_2 < \infty$ with
$$c_1 T^2 \;\le\; N(T) \;\le\; c_2 T^2 \quad\text{for all sufficiently large } T?$$

Equivalently, can one perturb an integrable Hamiltonian system so as to produce examples in which the number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits grows precisely quadratically (and not faster) in the period?
artifact.status_search_result: Standard literature on Hamiltonian perturbation theory (KAM, Poincaré–Birkhoff, near-resonance analysis) discusses persistence and multiplicity of periodic orbits, but a direct web search did not surface a definitive construction giving exactly quadratic (matching upper and lower bounds) growth of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits via perturbations of integrable systems, nor a proof of impossibility. The status appears unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian Perturbation Theory (and Transition to Chaos)
status_evidence.snippet: KAM theory and complementary results describe the persistence of invariant tori and behavior of trajectories under small perturbations of integrable Hamiltonians.
status_evidence.claim: General perturbation theory exists but does not directly produce sharp quadratic growth examples for primitive periodic orbits.

status_evidence.title: Periodic perturbations of Hamiltonian systems
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and multiplicity of periodic solutions via Poincaré–Birkhoff theorems applied to periodic perturbations of completely integrable systems.
status_evidence.claim: Multiplicity results are available but do not pin down exact quadratic asymptotics for the counting function.
